The skin changes (Gherkin for code, circuit-block Given/When/Then\\nfor electronics, request/response for an API); the skeleton never does.\\n\\n**This skill ships working machinery, not just doctrine.** If a repo has no card\\nsystem, install it — don't hand-write prose that evaporates with the conversation.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## DO THIS FIRST — is the machinery present?\\n\\n```bash\\nls features/*.feature 2>/dev/null | head -3   # cards exist?\\ngit config core.hooksPath                     # should print .githooks\\n```\\n\\n**No cards / no hooks → install, then card.** One command, idempotent, never commits:\\n\\n```bash\\n~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/install.sh            # current repo, features/\\n~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/install.sh --target /path/to/repo \\\\\\n    --cards-dir features --title \\\"Foo — Feature Reference\\\"\\n```\\n\\nIt drops into the repo:\\n\\n| Path | What it is |\\n|---|---|\\n| `features/print-card.py` | cards → `README.md` + printable `dist/` |\\n| `features/gen-status.py` | cards → `STATUS.md` (the derived test matrix) |\\n| `features/gen-sessions.py` | Codex transcripts → `SESSIONS.generated.md` |\\n| `features/cards.conf` | per-repo knobs (title, source extensions, exclusions) |\\n| `features/TEMPLATE.feature.txt` | the house-style skeleton to copy |\\n| `features/INDEX.md` | the commit ⇄ card map (the one hand-kept file) |\\n| `.githooks/pre-commit` + `post-merge` + `report-card-stamp.sh` | the stamp engine |\\n| `.githooks/pre-commit.local` | repo-local jobs — **yours, never clobbered on reinstall** |\\n| `core.hooksPath = .githooks` | set for this clone (git won't auto-run committed hooks) |\\n\\nThen, **every commit onward, with zero effort:** a diff touching a card's `# WATCH:`\\nsymbols stamps a dated RESULT-LOG line into that card *in the same commit*, and a\\nstaged card regenerates `STATUS.md` / `README.md` / `SESSIONS.generated.md` and stages\\nthem too. Mapping is **by symbol, not filename** — touching an unrelated part of a\\nshared file does not tag every card.\\n\\nAlready installed elsewhere and want the engine refreshed? Re-run `install.sh`; it\\noverwrites the canonical hooks + generators and keeps `pre-commit.local`, `cards.conf`,\\n`INDEX.md`, and every card. `--force` to overwrite those too.\\n\\n## Then: write the card (the same motion as the build)\\n\\n1. `cp features/TEMPLATE.feature.txt features/<name>.feature` and fill it in.\\n2. Write `features/<name>.session.md` — the spawning conversation, faithful not\\n   flattering, with the mandatory **How to get back** block.\\n3. Back-link the innards: `// REPORT-CARD >> features/<name>.feature` (comment syntax\\n   of that language).\\n4. Set the card's `# WATCH:` line to the symbols it owns — that's the hook contract.\\n5. Enrol it in `features/INDEX.md`.\\n6. `python3 features/print-card.py --readme` (and `--all` for printable `dist/`).\\n7. Commit. The hooks do the rest.\\n\\n**House style, grade ladder, banned anti-patterns:** `reference/house-style.md`.\\n**Why the format is shaped this way:** `reference/wiki-pattern.md`.\\n\\n## Just report back to me (works WITHOUT git)\\n\\n```bash\\n~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/report.sh --target ~/work/foo\\n```\\n\\nRegenerates every derived view and prints an honest summary: card count, scenario\\ncount, grades in use, and the three failure modes that otherwise stay silent —\\ncards with **no `# WATCH:` line** (the hooks can never stamp them), cards whose\\ngrade is written as a **trailing comment** instead of a Gherkin tag (no generator\\ncounts it, so they show as ungraded), and cards with **no `.session.md`** (broken\\ntriad). Finds the card home automatically (`features/`, `cards/`, `docs/cards`).\\n\\n**Git is optional.** Cards, generators and all derived views work on a plain\\nfolder — `install.sh` detects a non-git target, installs everything except the\\nhooks, and says so. Only RESULT-LOG *stamping* needs git, because it has to know\\nwhich symbols a diff touched. In a non-git folder you run `report.sh` yourself\\ninstead of a commit doing it for you.\\n\\n## cards.conf keys\\n\\n| Key | Effect |\\n|---|---|\\n| `title` | heading of the generated reference |\\n| `readme_file` | target for `--readme` (default `README.md`) — **set this if `features/README.md` is hand-written**, or it gets clobbered |\\n| `source_ext` | extensions recognised as \\\"innards\\\" in a `# cite:` line |\\n| `meta_prefix` | card-name prefixes grouped as meta/process cards |\\n| `exclude` | cards kept out of `STATUS.md` (rollups, host-side tooling) |\\n| `readme_exclude` | cards hidden from the reference entirely (rare) |\\n| `grade_map` | translate a repo's OWN grade words into canonical tiers, e.g. `@untested-in-renoise:@runtime-untested, @built:@code-verified` — the project keeps its vocabulary AND gets a correct matrix |\\n| `runtime_label` / `hardware_label` / `status_note` | STATUS.md column labels + note |\\n| `sessions_file` | session-registry filename (default `SESSIONS.generated.md`) |\\n| `project_dirs` | extra paths whose Codex transcripts belong to this repo |\\n\\n## Card dialects — indented banners are legal\\n\\nSome repos put the banner **inside** the `Feature:` block, indented (Paketti does).\\nThe stamp engine matches `# WATCH:` / `RESULT-LOG >>` at **line start with leading\\nwhitespace allowed**, so both dialects stamp, and the inserted line copies the\\nmarker's own indentation. What is still rejected is a *mid-sentence* mention of the\\nmarker in prose, so a card describing the convention can't opt itself in.\\n\\nA strict column-0 anchor is what made every Paketti card a silent no-op for months —\\nhooks installed, running, stamping nothing, no error. If cards aren't being stamped,\\nrun `report.sh` before assuming the hooks are broken.\\n\\n## Verification commands\\n\\n```bash\\npython3 features/print-card.py --readme     # regenerate the feature reference\\npython3 features/print-card.py --all        # per-card dist/ (pure Gherkin + printable)\\npython3 features/gen-status.py              # regenerate the test matrix\\npython3 features/gen-sessions.py            # regenerate the session registry\\nrtfc features/dist/<name>.card.md           # printable card → RTF clipboard\\n```\\n\\nAll are dependency-free Apple-native python3, deterministic (no timestamps embedded,\\nso no commit churn), and resolve the card home from `--cards-dir` → `$REPORT_CARDS_DIR`\\n→ the script's own directory.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## The four properties (every card, every domain)\\n\\n1. **Verifiable claims** — condition → action → expected result.\\n   `Given <state>, When <action>, Then <measurable outcome>`.\\n2. **Linked to the innards** — each claim cites the exact parts that satisfy it\\n   (proc + line + commit; component refdes + node; file + function).\\n3. **Honestly graded** — one tag per claim. The grade is the anti-lying mechanism.\\n   `@designed` `@built` `@build-verified` `@sim-verified` `@runtime-verified`\\n   `@hw-verified` `@untested` `@hw-untested` `@todo` `@stock`.\\n   Untested is untested. **Never grade up to look finished.**\\n4. **Two-way** — the innards carry a greppable back-link to the card, so the wiki is\\n   bidirectional.\\n\\n## The triad — three legs, all cross-linked\\n\\n- **`<name>.feature` (the card)** — the spec: graded verifiable claims, each cited to\\n  its innards. The *what* + *why-as-grade*.\\n- **`<name>.session.md`** — the spawning conversation stored beside the card: the\\n  requests, refinements, corrections, rejected options, the \\\"no I didn't do it\\\"\\n  admissions. **Faithful, not flattering** — the grade's audit trail. This enables the\\n  **vibe diff**: across versions you diff the code, the card, AND the dialogue that\\n  drove each change. A card without its session can spawn the code but not the vibe —\\n  INCOMPLETE.\\n  **MANDATORY \\\"How to get back\\\" block** — transcript `file://` path, session ID,\\n  `Codex --resume <id>`, real date+timestamps pulled from the transcript (never\\n  fabricated; if unconfirmable, say so). `gen-sessions.py` discovers these repo-wide.\\n  **MANDATORY bundle, don't just link** — a `file://` link rots the moment the\\n  `.jsonl` moves. Copy the raw transcript beside the card as\\n  `<name>.transcript.jsonl` (lossless) plus a readable `<name>.transcript.md`. The\\n  curated `.session.md` is the audit; the bundled transcript is the source.\\n- **RESULT block** (card header) — what actually shipped: feature commit(s), the PR if\\n  any (\\\"direct-push, no PR\\\" when none), card-authoring commit(s), files changed.\\n  Verify delivery by first-parent ancestry — don't guess; watch duplicate PR numbers\\n  across forks. The hooks maintain the running RESULT-LOG under it.\\n\\nThree legs cross-linked ⇒ the wiki is rebuildable straight from git: load one card →\\nspec + rationale + diff, no re-reading raw source.\\n\\n## The card is a generative seed (it comes first)\\n\\nThe card opens with a **WHAT THIS CARD SPAWNS** preamble because it spawns three spaces:\\n\\n- **Codespace** = the file structure — the card's own files plus the innards layout it\\n  cites. From the card you can scaffold or re-derive the code.\\n- **Thinkspace** = the reasoning — held in the `.session` (wrong turns included). Also\\n  what the vibe diff diffs.\\n- **Areaspace** = the domain boundary — what the unit owns and must NOT touch, so\\n  re-spawning stays in-bounds. Make it verifiable with a `@stock` \\\"must not break\\\"\\n  scenario.\\n\\n`card ⇒ codespace + areaspace`; `session ⇒ thinkspace`.\\n\\n## Tests → Features → automatic index (never hand-typed)\\n\\nThe whole point is that **code conveys its own verified status** — a behaviour is\\nwritten ONCE and every status view derives from it:\\n\\n1. **Tests ARE the Features.** A verifiable claim lives once as a graded `Scenario`;\\n   its `@grade` tags **are** its test status.\\n2. **Features become the index.** The status view is GENERATED from those tags, run\\n   automatically by the pre-commit hook, committed alongside the card.\\n3. **So anyone can confirm** with zero manual labour: tested or not, at what level, and\\n   where it links (card → innards → commits → session).\\n\\n**Banned anti-pattern:** hand-maintaining a parallel \\\"what's tested\\\" list. If you catch\\nyourself typing `runtime-verified` into an index, stop — change the card's tag and let\\nthe index regenerate. A derived view cannot disagree with its source; a hand-kept one\\ndrifts and lies. Generated files carry a `DO NOT EDIT — generated` header.\\n\\n## Relationship to Convey (`~/work/convey`)\\n\\n**This skill is the DOCTRINE + SKIN SYSTEM + portable tooling. Convey is the larger\\nENGINE.** A report card IS a Convey \\\"Underlying Principle\\\" — a `principles/NNNN-slug/`\\nfolder bound to git. The hooks shipped here are Convey's canonical stamp engine, which\\nis why `install.sh` and `convey hooks install --target .` are interchangeable for the\\nhook half.\\n\\nMapping (full detail in `~/work/convey/docs/DOCTRINE.md`):\\n\\n- **Emit a card** = `convey new \\\"<title>\\\" --target <folder> --skin <code|circuit|api|media>`.\\n- **`.feature`** = stage 1 *Describe*; `convey verify` reconciles the declared grade\\n  with the actual run and **flags optimism** (OPTIMISTIC / UNVERIFIED) — the anti-lying\\n  mechanism, automated. Where no runner exists it reports UNRUN and keeps the declared\\n  grade (never fakes a pass).\\n- **`.session`** = stage 2 *Sessions* + `convey bundle` copies the lossless transcript\\n  beside the card and fills \\\"How to get back\\\".\\n- **RESULT** = stage 3 *Done* (git-derived) + stage 5 *Change*.\\n- **Two-way back-link** = `convey backlink`. **The wiki** = `convey atlas`.\\n\\nUse Convey where it's installed; use `scripts/install.sh` for any repo (or machine)\\nwhere it isn't. The four properties and three legs are identical either way.\\n\\n## The card is conversable\\n\\nThe `.feature` is compact distilled text with the bundled session as lossless backing,\\nso you can hand it to a `file-to-text` → LLM reader and *talk to it*:\\n\\n```bash\\ncard converse <name>           # resolve by name + fm-converse it (Apple on-device LLM)\\ncard converse <name> --full    # converse over the full bundled transcript\\ncard bundle <name>             # copy + render the spawning session beside the card\\ncard list | show | path        # browse cards\\n```\\n\\n`card` lives at `~/work/apple/bin/card`. This is *why* the full session must be\\nbundled, not merely linked — an `fm-converse` session can't follow a dead `file://`\\nlink, but it can read a sibling file.\\n\\n**The universality corollary.** The card is the *same skeleton for every file format*,\\nso the underlying principle of ANY file can be read INTO a card: take a `.lua` tool, a\\n`.mp4`, a `.sch`, a `.pdf`, a `.wav` — distill what it *does* and *why* into graded\\nGiven/When/Then claims cited to its innards, bundle the session that produced it, and\\nthe card becomes the universal, conversable lens on that file.\\n\\n## Domain skins (same skeleton)\\n\\n- **Code** — Gherkin `.feature`; scenarios cite `FILE.ext Proc (~line)` + commit; tags\\n  for status; back-link comment in the source.\\n- **Electronics / circuits** — one card per block. `Given Vin = 5.0V, When EN goes\\n  high, Then Vout settles to 3.3V ±2% within 200µs`; cite parts (`U1 AP2112`, divider\\n  `R3/R4`, `Cout C7`); grade `@sim-verified @hw-untested`. A whole circuit \\\"already\\n  contains its report card\\\" = each block ships its card; building the circuit is\\n  composing cards; the top card is the sum of sub-cards; schematic ⇄ card back-link.\\n  Pairs with `circuitjs1` / `schematic-to-circuitjs`.\\n- **API / pipeline / signal chain** — claim = request→response / input→artifact /\\n  source→processed; cite the endpoint/stage/device; grade by where it's verified.\\n\\n## Backfilling click-back into an existing session file (retrofit)\\n\\nWhen a card/session predates the click-back requirement, identify the spawning\\ntranscript by **content, never by guess**:\\n\\n1. `cd ~/.Codex/projects/<sanitized-cwd>/` (one `.jsonl` per session), or just run\\n   `gen-sessions.py` which does the discovery repo-wide.\\n2. Count fixed-string hits per transcript on distinctive strings from the work:\\n   `for f in *.jsonl; do echo \\\"$(grep -cF -e \\\"PTN0003\\\" -e \\\"Lackluster\\\" \\\"$f\\\")  $f\\\"; done`\\n   Use `grep -F` / `rg -F` — **never** a regex with `.*` between literals\\n   (catastrophic-backtracking ban). Confirm with a second distinct probe (65 vs 11 hits\\n   is decisive; 7 vs 6 is not).\\n3. Pull the window: first/last `\\\"timestamp\\\"`; convert UTC → local.\\n4. Add the **How to get back** block, including an \\\"identified by content, not guessed\\\"\\n   note with the hit count and a \\\"Backfilled: <date>\\\" line.\\n5. **Honesty:** never fabricate a session ID. If nothing decisively matches, say so.\\n\\n## The one honest caveat\\n\\nFor domains with no test runner (16-bit TASM assembly, a bench circuit before hardware\\nexists), the card's claims are *verifiable-in-principle* — a disciplined human/LLM\\nchecklist and session command until automation glue exists. The wiki value (persistent,\\ncompounding, faithful, loadable-as-command, git-rebuildable) holds on day one\\nregardless of whether the automation is ever written.\\n\\n---\\n\\nGlobal rule: His words: the nugget is the report card itself, and it can be **whitelabeled** so that \\\"creating a circuit in an electronics system already contains the report card of what the innards of it are.\\\" He chose to make it a global rule.\\n\\n### The four properties of a card\\n\\n1. **Verifiable claims** — condition → action → expected result (Given / When / Then; for hardware: given these inputs, when this happens, then this measured output).\\n2. **Linked to the innards** — each claim cites the exact parts that satisfy it (proc + line + commit; component + node; file + function).\\n3. **Honestly graded** — `@designed` / `@built` / `@sim-verified` / `@hw-verified` / `@untested` / `@todo`. Verify delivery accurately (first-parent ancestry: direct-to-main vs PR-merged) — don't guess; watch duplicate PR numbers across forks.\\n\\nThree legs cross-linked ⇒ the wiki is **rebuildable straight from git**: load one card → spec + rationale + diff without re-reading raw source.\\n\\n### The card is a generative seed (it comes first)\\n\\nThe card spawns three spaces, so it carries an explicit \\\"WHAT THIS CARD SPAWNS\\\" preamble:\\n- **Codespace** = the file structure (the card's own files + the innards layout it cites).\\n- **Thinkspace** = the reasoning (held in the `.session`; also what the vibe diff diffs).\\n- **Areaspace** = the domain boundary — what the unit owns and what it must NOT touch — so re-spawning stays in-bounds.\\n\\n### How to apply\\n\\n1. Cards then regenerate their own `README.md` / `STATUS.md` and stamp their own RESULT-LOGs on every commit. **A card written as chat prose is work Esa never gets back** — that was the failure mode until 2026-08-14, when the machinery was isolated out of `esaruoho/impulse-tracker` into the skill.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 🔴 MANDATORY: `cp` AND `mv` ARE ALIASED TO `-iv` ON ESA'S MACHINE — A SCRIPTED OVERWRITE WILL HANG, NOT FAIL\\n\\n**Esa's `~/.bash_profile` (lines 1271–1272) sets:**\\n\\n```bash\\nalias cp=\\\"cp -iv\\\"\\nalias mv=\\\"mv -iv\\\"\\n```\\n\\n**The Codex Bash tool initializes its shell from that profile, so these aliases ARE live in every Bash call I make.** `rm` is *not* aliased — only `cp` and `mv`.\\n\\n### What actually goes wrong — TWO failure shapes, and the quiet one is worse\\n\\n`-i` means *prompt before overwriting an existing file*. In a tool call there is nobody to answer, and what happens next depends on what stdin is attached to:\\n\\n- **It blocks.** If stdin stays open (e.g. the call also used a heredoc), `cp` waits forever on `overwrite <file>? (y/n [n])`. The harness times out and backgrounds the call, which reads like a mysterious hang, and an orphan process sits on stdin until killed.\\n- **It silently declines.** If stdin is at EOF, `cp` takes the default answer — *no* — and returns non-zero. **Verified 2026-08-08: it can do this printing NOTHING at all.** No prompt text, no error, no output. The destination simply still holds its old content.\\n\\nBoth shapes leave the **destination untouched** and any `&&` chain unexecuted. The silent one is the dangerous one, because at a glance the call looks like it worked.\\n\\n**Diagnostic:** if a Bash call inexplicably backgrounds/times out, read the output file and look for `overwrite <path>? (y/n [n])`. And after *any* scripted copy, if correctness matters, verify the destination actually changed (`wc -l`, `md5`, a `grep` for something only the new version has) rather than trusting exit status.\\n\\n### The rule\\n\\n1. **Prefer the `Write` / `Edit` tools over shell copies for file content.** They never prompt, and they keep the harness's file-state tracking correct. Reach for the shell only when it is genuinely a filesystem operation.\\n2. **When you must copy in a script or tool call, bypass the alias explicitly.** All four verified working on 2026-08-08 (destination actually changed):\\n   - `command cp SRC DST` — cleanest, bypasses alias lookup entirely ✅\\n   - `/bin/cp SRC DST` — absolute path, same effect ✅\\n   - `\\\\cp SRC DST` — backslash suppresses alias expansion ✅\\n   - `cat SRC > DST` — when the goal is really \\\"make DST have SRC's content\\\" ✅\\n3. **`cp -f` DOES NOT WORK — do not use it as the bypass.** Verified twice on 2026-08-08: `cp -f src dst` expands to `cp -iv -f src dst` and *still* declines the overwrite, leaving the destination stale. The BSD man-page claim that \\\"the last of `-f`/`-i`/`-n` takes precedence\\\" does not hold here. Same for the un-bypassed plain `cp` and plain `mv` — both left `dst=OLD`.\\n4. **Same bypasses for `mv`** — `command mv`, `/bin/mv`, or `\\\\mv`. Verified: plain `mv` leaves the destination stale; `command mv` works.\\n5. **Never chain an un-bypassed `cp`/`mv` with `&&`.** If it prompts or declines, everything downstream silently does not happen.\\n6. **Gotcha — a wrapper hides the alias.** Aliases are only expanded when the word is in *command* position, so `timeout 4 cp src dst`, `xargs cp`, `find -exec cp`, and `sudo cp` all get the raw `/bin/cp` with no `-i`. That is why some scripted copies work and others do not. Do not use this as the bypass (it is accidental); just know it when explaining behaviour.\\n7. **Do not \\\"fix\\\" this by editing `~/.bash_profile`.** The aliases are a deliberate safety net Esa set for his own interactive use (from natelandau's bash_profile). My tooling adapts to his environment, not the reverse.\\n\\n### Why this rule exists\\n\\n2026-08-07, ParaEQ Symphonic session: I built a new `SymphonicHarmonics.h` in a scratchpad file and ran `cat >> head.h <<'EOF' … EOF && cp head.h Source/SymphonicHarmonics.h && wc -l …`. The call timed out into the background, `wc -l` never ran, and `Source/SymphonicHarmonics.h` still held the **old 757-line** version while I believed the 811-line rewrite had landed. I only caught it because the line count looked wrong. A delayed `killed` task-notification for that same command arrived much later in the session, long after I had worked around it — noise that cost a second round of investigation.\\n\\nCost: one wasted tool call, one stale-file near-miss on a file I was actively rewriting, and a confusing orphan notification.\\n\\n### Single-sentence statement\\n\\n`cp` and `mv` are aliased to `-iv` in Esa's bash_profile and the harness shell inherits them, so in any scripted or tool-call context use `command cp` / `command mv` / `\\\\cp` / `cat SRC > DST` (or the `Write` tool) and never `cp -f` — an un-bypassed overwrite either hangs on a prompt or silently declines with no output at all, leaving the destination stale and the rest of the `&&` chain unexecuted.\\n\\n--- project-doc ---\\n\\n\\n<!-- agenttrail -->\\n## agenttrail plan convention\\nMaintain PLAN.md as the living plan. The card is not documentation\\n> bolted on after — it is the durable artifact the work is born with, the SEED the\\n> work spawns from, and the honest, graded, two-way-linked account of what the unit\\n> does and which of its innards do it. The skin changes (Gherkin for code, circuit-block Given/When/Then\\nfor electronics, request/response for an API); the skeleton never does.\\n\\n**This skill ships working machinery, not just doctrine.** If a repo has no card\\nsystem, install it — don't hand-write prose that evaporates with the conversation.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## DO THIS FIRST — is the machinery present?\\n\\n```bash\\nls features/*.feature 2>/dev/null | head -3   # cards exist?\\ngit config core.hooksPath                     # should print .githooks\\n```\\n\\n**No cards / no hooks → install, then card.** One command, idempotent, never commits:\\n\\n```bash\\n~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/install.sh            # current repo, features/\\n~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/install.sh --target /path/to/repo \\\\\\n    --cards-dir features --title \\\"Foo — Feature Reference\\\"\\n```\\n\\nIt drops into the repo:\\n\\n| Path | What it is |\\n|---|---|\\n| `features/print-card.py` | cards → `README.md` + printable `dist/` |\\n| `features/gen-status.py` | cards → `STATUS.md` (the derived test matrix) |\\n| `features/gen-sessions.py` | Codex transcripts → `SESSIONS.generated.md` |\\n| `features/cards.conf` | per-repo knobs (title, source extensions, exclusions) |\\n| `features/TEMPLATE.feature.txt` | the house-style skeleton to copy |\\n| `features/INDEX.md` | the commit ⇄ card map (the one hand-kept file) |\\n| `.githooks/pre-commit` + `post-merge` + `report-card-stamp.sh` | the stamp engine |\\n| `.githooks/pre-commit.local` | repo-local jobs — **yours, never clobbered on reinstall** |\\n| `core.hooksPath = .githooks` | set for this clone (git won't auto-run committed hooks) |\\n\\nThen, **every commit onward, with zero effort:** a diff touching a card's `# WATCH:`\\nsymbols stamps a dated RESULT-LOG line into that card *in the same commit*, and a\\nstaged card regenerates `STATUS.md` / `README.md` / `SESSIONS.generated.md` and stages\\nthem too. Mapping is **by symbol, not filename** — touching an unrelated part of a\\nshared file does not tag every card.\\n\\nAlready installed elsewhere and want the engine refreshed? Finds the card home automatically (`features/`, `cards/`, `docs/cards`).\\n\\n**Git is optional.** Cards, generators and all derived views work on a plain\\nfolder — `install.sh` detects a non-git target, installs everything except the\\nhooks, and says so. Only RESULT-LOG *stamping* needs git, because it has to know\\nwhich symbols a diff touched. In a non-git folder you run `report.sh` yourself\\ninstead of a commit doing it for you.\\n\\n## cards.conf keys\\n\\n| Key | Effect |\\n|---|---|\\n| `title` | heading of the generated reference |\\n| `readme_file` | target for `--readme` (default `README.md`) — **set this if `features/README.md` is hand-written**, or it gets clobbered |\\n| `source_ext` | extensions recognised as \\\"innards\\\" in a `# cite:` line |\\n| `meta_prefix` | card-name prefixes grouped as meta/process cards |\\n| `exclude` | cards kept out of `STATUS.md` (rollups, host-side tooling) |\\n| `readme_exclude` | cards hidden from the reference entirely (rare) |\\n| `grade_map` | translate a repo's OWN grade words into canonical tiers, e.g. `@untested-in-renoise:@runtime-untested, @built:@code-verified` — the project keeps its vocabulary AND gets a correct matrix |\\n| `runtime_label` / `hardware_label` / `status_note` | STATUS.md column labels + note |\\n| `sessions_file` | session-registry filename (default `SESSIONS.generated.md`) |\\n| `project_dirs` | extra paths whose Codex transcripts belong to this repo |\\n\\n## Card dialects — indented banners are legal\\n\\nSome repos put the banner **inside** the `Feature:` block, indented (Paketti does).\\nThe stamp engine matches `# WATCH:` / `RESULT-LOG >>` at **line start with leading\\nwhitespace allowed**, so both dialects stamp, and the inserted line copies the\\nmarker's own indentation. What is still rejected is a *mid-sentence* mention of the\\nmarker in prose, so a card describing the convention can't opt itself in.\\n\\nA strict column-0 anchor is what made every Paketti card a silent no-op for months —\\nhooks installed, running, stamping nothing, no error. If cards aren't being stamped,\\nrun `report.sh` before assuming the hooks are broken.\\n\\n## Verification commands\\n\\n```bash\\npython3 features/print-card.py --readme     # regenerate the feature reference\\npython3 features/print-card.py --all        # per-card dist/ (pure Gherkin + printable)\\npython3 features/gen-status.py              # regenerate the test matrix\\npython3 features/gen-sessions.py            # regenerate the session registry\\nrtfc features/dist/<name>.card.md           # printable card → RTF clipboard\\n```\\n\\nAll are dependency-free Apple-native python3, deterministic (no timestamps embedded,\\nso no commit churn), and resolve the card home from `--cards-dir` → `$REPORT_CARDS_DIR`\\n→ the script's own directory.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## The four properties (every card, every domain)\\n\\n1. **Verifiable claims** — condition → action → expected result.\\n   `Given <state>, When <action>, Then <measurable outcome>`.\\n2. **Linked to the innards** — each claim cites the exact parts that satisfy it\\n   (proc + line + commit; component refdes + node; file + function).\\n3. **Honestly graded** — one tag per claim. The grade is the anti-lying mechanism.\\n   `@designed` `@built` `@build-verified` `@sim-verified` `@runtime-verified`\\n   `@hw-verified` `@untested` `@hw-untested` `@todo` `@stock`.\\n   Untested is untested. **Never grade up to look finished.**\\n4. **Two-way** — the innards carry a greppable back-link to the card, so the wiki is\\n   bidirectional.\\n\\n## The triad — three legs, all cross-linked\\n\\n- **`<name>.feature` (the card)** — the spec: graded verifiable claims, each cited to\\n  its innards. The *what* + *why-as-grade*.\\n- **`<name>.session.md`** — the spawning conversation stored beside the card: the\\n  requests, refinements, corrections, rejected options, the \\\"no I didn't do it\\\"\\n  admissions. **Faithful, not flattering** — the grade's audit trail. This enables the\\n  **vibe diff**: across versions you diff the code, the card, AND the dialogue that\\n  drove each change. A card without its session can spawn the code but not the vibe —\\n  INCOMPLETE.\\n  **MANDATORY \\\"How to get back\\\" block** — transcript `file://` path, session ID,\\n  `Codex --resume <id>`, real date+timestamps pulled from the transcript (never\\n  fabricated; if unconfirmable, say so). `gen-sessions.py` discovers these repo-wide.\\n  **MANDATORY bundle, don't just link** — a `file://` link rots the moment the\\n  `.jsonl` moves. Copy the raw transcript beside the card as\\n  `<name>.transcript.jsonl` (lossless) plus a readable `<name>.transcript.md`. The\\n  curated `.session.md` is the audit; the bundled transcript is the source.\\n- **RESULT block** (card header) — what actually shipped: feature commit(s), the PR if\\n  any (\\\"direct-push, no PR\\\" when none), card-authoring commit(s), files changed.\\n  Verify delivery by first-parent ancestry — don't guess; watch duplicate PR numbers\\n  across forks. The hooks maintain the running RESULT-LOG under it.\\n\\nThree legs cross-linked ⇒ the wiki is rebuildable straight from git: load one card →\\nspec + rationale + diff, no re-reading raw source.\\n\\n## The card is a generative seed (it comes first)\\n\\nThe card opens with a **WHAT THIS CARD SPAWNS** preamble because it spawns three spaces:\\n\\n- **Codespace** = the file structure — the card's own files plus the innards layout it\\n  cites. From the card you can scaffold or re-derive the code.\\n- **Thinkspace** = the reasoning — held in the `.session` (wrong turns included). Also\\n  what the vibe diff diffs.\\n- **Areaspace** = the domain boundary — what the unit owns and must NOT touch, so\\n  re-spawning stays in-bounds. Make it verifiable with a `@stock` \\\"must not break\\\"\\n  scenario.\\n\\n`card ⇒ codespace + areaspace`; `session ⇒ thinkspace`.\\n\\n## Tests → Features → automatic index (never hand-typed)\\n\\nThe whole point is that **code conveys its own verified status** — a behaviour is\\nwritten ONCE and every status view derives from it:\\n\\n1. **Tests ARE the Features.** A verifiable claim lives once as a graded `Scenario`;\\n   its `@grade` tags **are** its test status.\\n2. **Features become the index.** The status view is GENERATED from those tags, run\\n   automatically by the pre-commit hook, committed alongside the card.\\n3. **So anyone can confirm** with zero manual labour: tested or not, at what level, and\\n   where it links (card → innards → commits → session).\\n\\n**Banned anti-pattern:** hand-maintaining a parallel \\\"what's tested\\\" list. If you catch\\nyourself typing `runtime-verified` into an index, stop — change the card's tag and let\\nthe index regenerate. A derived view cannot disagree with its source; a hand-kept one\\ndrifts and lies. Generated files carry a `DO NOT EDIT — generated` header.\\n\\n## Relationship to Convey (`~/work/convey`)\\n\\n**This skill is the DOCTRINE + SKIN SYSTEM + portable tooling. Convey is the larger\\nENGINE.** A report card IS a Convey \\\"Underlying Principle\\\" — a `principles/NNNN-slug/`\\nfolder bound to git. The hooks shipped here are Convey's canonical stamp engine, which\\nis why `install.sh` and `convey hooks install --target .` are interchangeable for the\\nhook half.\\n\\nMapping (full detail in `~/work/convey/docs/DOCTRINE.md`):\\n\\n- **Emit a card** = `convey new \\\"<title>\\\" --target <folder> --skin <code|circuit|api|media>`.\\n- **`.feature`** = stage 1 *Describe*; `convey verify` reconciles the declared grade\\n  with the actual run and **flags optimism** (OPTIMISTIC / UNVERIFIED) — the anti-lying\\n  mechanism, automated. Where no runner exists it reports UNRUN and keeps the declared\\n  grade (never fakes a pass).\\n- **`.session`** = stage 2 *Sessions* + `convey bundle` copies the lossless transcript\\n  beside the card and fills \\\"How to get back\\\".\\n- **RESULT** = stage 3 *Done* (git-derived) + stage 5 *Change*.\\n- **Two-way back-link** = `convey backlink`. **The wiki** = `convey atlas`.\\n\\nUse Convey where it's installed; use `scripts/install.sh` for any repo (or machine)\\nwhere it isn't. The four properties and three legs are identical either way.\\n\\n## The card is conversable\\n\\nThe `.feature` is compact distilled text with the bundled session as lossless backing,\\nso you can hand it to a `file-to-text` → LLM reader and *talk to it*:\\n\\n```bash\\ncard converse <name>           # resolve by name + fm-converse it (Apple on-device LLM)\\ncard converse <name> --full    # converse over the full bundled transcript\\ncard bundle <name>             # copy + render the spawning session beside the card\\ncard list | show | path        # browse cards\\n```\\n\\n`card` lives at `~/work/apple/bin/card`. This is *why* the full session must be\\nbundled, not merely linked — an `fm-converse` session can't follow a dead `file://`\\nlink, but it can read a sibling file.\\n\\n**The universality corollary.** The card is the *same skeleton for every file format*,\\nso the underlying principle of ANY file can be read INTO a card: take a `.lua` tool, a\\n`.mp4`, a `.sch`, a `.pdf`, a `.wav` — distill what it *does* and *why* into graded\\nGiven/When/Then claims cited to its innards, bundle the session that produced it, and\\nthe card becomes the universal, conversable lens on that file.\\n\\n## Domain skins (same skeleton)\\n\\n- **Code** — Gherkin `.feature`; scenarios cite `FILE.ext Proc (~line)` + commit; tags\\n  for status; back-link comment in the source.\\n- **Electronics / circuits** — one card per block. `Given Vin = 5.0V, When EN goes\\n  high, Then Vout settles to 3.3V ±2% within 200µs`; cite parts (`U1 AP2112`, divider\\n  `R3/R4`, `Cout C7`); grade `@sim-verified @hw-untested`. A whole circuit \\\"already\\n  contains its report card\\\" = each block ships its card; building the circuit is\\n  composing cards; the top card is the sum of sub-cards; schematic ⇄ card back-link.\\n  Pairs with `circuitjs1` / `schematic-to-circuitjs`.\\n- **API / pipeline / signal chain** — claim = request→response / input→artifact /\\n  source→processed; cite the endpoint/stage/device; grade by where it's verified.\\n\\n## Backfilling click-back into an existing session file (retrofit)\\n\\nWhen a card/session predates the click-back requirement, identify the spawning\\ntranscript by **content, never by guess**:\\n\\n1. `cd ~/.Codex/projects/<sanitized-cwd>/` (one `.jsonl` per session), or just run\\n   `gen-sessions.py` which does the discovery repo-wide.\\n2. Count fixed-string hits per transcript on distinctive strings from the work:\\n   `for f in *.jsonl; do echo \\\"$(grep -cF -e \\\"PTN0003\\\" -e \\\"Lackluster\\\" \\\"$f\\\")  $f\\\"; done`\\n   Use `grep -F` / `rg -F` — **never** a regex with `.*` between literals\\n   (catastrophic-backtracking ban). Confirm with a second distinct probe (65 vs 11 hits\\n   is decisive; 7 vs 6 is not).\\n3. Pull the window: first/last `\\\"timestamp\\\"`; convert UTC → local.\\n4. Add the **How to get back** block, including an \\\"identified by content, not guessed\\\"\\n   note with the hit count and a \\\"Backfilled: <date>\\\" line.\\n5. **Honesty:** never fabricate a session ID. If nothing decisively matches, say so.\\n\\n## The one honest caveat\\n\\nFor domains with no test runner (16-bit TASM assembly, a bench circuit before hardware\\nexists), the card's claims are *verifiable-in-principle* — a disciplined human/LLM\\nchecklist and session command until automation glue exists. ---
name: report-card
description: Emit a report card for any built unit — code feature, circuit block, subsystem, API, pipeline, signal chain — AND install the machinery that keeps it alive. A report card is the triad {.feature spec + .session conversation + RESULT (commits/PR/files)} born WITH the thing, graded honestly, linked both ways to its innards, and acting as the seed the work spawns from. Ships working tooling: an installer that drops card generators + self-stamping git hooks into any repo, so cards regenerate their own README/STATUS and stamp their own RESULT-LOGs. Use when building/shipping a unit that should carry its own durable, graded, session-backed description, or when a repo has no card system yet. Triggers on "report card", "report on this", "make a card for this", "card this feature/circuit", "whitelabel the card", "vibe diff", or finishing a unit of work that should self-document.
domain: cross-domain
version: 2.0.0
tags: [report-card, gherkin, feature, session, vibe-diff, wiki, traceability, electronics, circuits, honesty, seed, git-hooks, tooling]
---

# Report Card

> Building a unit of anything emits its report card. The card is not documentation
> bolted on after — it is the durable artifact the work is born with, the SEED the
> work spawns from, and the honest, graded, two-way-linked account of what the unit
> does and which of its innards do it. A unit shipped without its card is incomplete.

Domain-agnostic. The skin changes (Gherkin for code, circuit-block Given/When/Then
for electronics, request/response for an API); the skeleton never does.

**This skill ships working machinery, not just doctrine.** If a repo has no card
system, install it — don't hand-write prose that evaporates with the conversation.

---

## DO THIS FIRST — is the machinery present?

```bash
ls features/*.feature 2>/dev/null | head -3   # cards exist?
git config core.hooksPath                     # should print .githooks
```

**No cards / no hooks → install, then card.** One command, idempotent, never commits:

```bash
~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/install.sh            # current repo, features/
~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/install.sh --target /path/to/repo \
    --cards-dir features --title "Foo — Feature Reference"
```

It drops into the repo:

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `features/print-card.py` | cards → `README.md` + printable `dist/` |
| `features/gen-status.py` | cards → `STATUS.md` (the derived test matrix) |
| `features/gen-sessions.py` | Codex transcripts → `SESSIONS.generated.md` |
| `features/cards.conf` | per-repo knobs (title, source extensions, exclusions) |
| `features/TEMPLATE.feature.txt` | the house-style skeleton to copy |
| `features/INDEX.md` | the commit ⇄ card map (the one hand-kept file) |
| `.githooks/pre-commit` + `post-merge` + `report-card-stamp.sh` | the stamp engine |
| `.githooks/pre-commit.local` | repo-local jobs — **yours, never clobbered on reinstall** |
| `core.hooksPath = .githooks` | set for this clone (git won't auto-run committed hooks) |

Then, **every commit onward, with zero effort:** a diff touching a card's `# WATCH:`
symbols stamps a dated RESULT-LOG line into that card *in the same commit*, and a
staged card regenerates `STATUS.md` / `README.md` / `SESSIONS.generated.md` and stages
them too. Mapping is **by symbol, not filename** — touching an unrelated part of a
shared file does not tag every card.

Already installed elsewhere and want the engine refreshed? Re-run `install.sh`; it
overwrites the canonical hooks + generators and keeps `pre-commit.local`, `cards.conf`,
`INDEX.md`, and every card. `--force` to overwrite those too.

## Then: write the card (the same motion as the build)

1. `cp features/TEMPLATE.feature.txt features/<name>.feature` and fill it in.
2. Write `features/<name>.session.md` — the spawning conversation, faithful not
   flattering, with the mandatory **How to get back** block.
3. Back-link the innards: `// REPORT-CARD >> features/<name>.feature` (comment syntax
   of that language).
4. Set the card's `# WATCH:` line to the symbols it owns — that's the hook contract.
5. Enrol it in `features/INDEX.md`.
6. `python3 features/print-card.py --readme` (and `--all` for printable `dist/`).
7. Commit. The hooks do the rest.

**House style, grade ladder, banned anti-patterns:** `reference/house-style.md`.
**Why the format is shaped this way:** `reference/wiki-pattern.md`.

## Just report back to me (works WITHOUT git)

```bash
~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/report.sh --target ~/work/foo
```

Regenerates every derived view and prints an honest summary: card count, scenario
count, grades in use, and the three failure modes that otherwise stay silent —
cards with **no `# WATCH:` line** (the hooks can never stamp them), cards whose
grade is written as a **trailing comment** instead of a Gherkin tag (no generator
counts it, so they show as ungraded), and cards with **no `.session.md`** (broken
triad). Finds the card home automatically (`features/`, `cards/`, `docs/cards`).

**Git is optional.** Cards, generators and all derived views work on a plain
folder — `install.sh` detects a non-git target, installs everything except the
hooks, and says so. Only RESULT-LOG *stamping* needs git, because it has to know
which symbols a diff touched. In a non-git folder you run `report.sh` yourself
instead of a commit doing it for you.

## cards.conf keys

| Key | Effect |
|---|---|
| `title` | heading of the generated reference |
| `readme_file` | target for `--readme` (default `README.md`) — **set this if `features/README.md` is hand-written**, or it gets clobbered |
| `source_ext` | extensions recognised as "innards" in a `# cite:` line |
| `meta_prefix` | card-name prefixes grouped as meta/process cards |
| `exclude` | cards kept out of `STATUS.md` (rollups, host-side tooling) |
| `readme_exclude` | cards hidden from the reference entirely (rare) |
| `grade_map` | translate a repo's OWN grade words into canonical tiers, e.g. `@untested-in-renoise:@runtime-untested, @built:@code-verified` — the project keeps its vocabulary AND gets a correct matrix |
| `runtime_label` / `hardware_label` / `status_note` | STATUS.md column labels + note |
| `sessions_file` | session-registry filename (default `SESSIONS.generated.md`) |
| `project_dirs` | extra paths whose Codex transcripts belong to this repo |

## Card dialects — indented banners are legal

Some repos put the banner **inside** the `Feature:` block, indented (Paketti does).
The stamp engine matches `# WATCH:` / `RESULT-LOG >>` at **line start with leading
whitespace allowed**, so both dialects stamp, and the inserted line copies the
marker's own indentation. What is still rejected is a *mid-sentence* mention of the
marker in prose, so a card describing the convention can't opt itself in.

A strict column-0 anchor is what made every Paketti card a silent no-op for months —
hooks installed, running, stamping nothing, no error. If cards aren't being stamped,
run `report.sh` before assuming the hooks are broken.

## Verification commands

```bash
python3 features/print-card.py --readme     # regenerate the feature reference
python3 features/print-card.py --all        # per-card dist/ (pure Gherkin + printable)
python3 features/gen-status.py              # regenerate the test matrix
python3 features/gen-sessions.py            # regenerate the session registry
rtfc features/dist/<name>.card.md           # printable card → RTF clipboard
```

All are dependency-free Apple-native python3, deterministic (no timestamps embedded,
so no commit churn), and resolve the card home from `--cards-dir` → `$REPORT_CARDS_DIR`
→ the script's own directory.

---

## The four properties (every card, every domain)

1. **Verifiable claims** — condition → action → expected result.
   `Given <state>, When <action>, Then <measurable outcome>`.
2. **Linked to the innards** — each claim cites the exact parts that satisfy it
   (proc + line + commit; component refdes + node; file + function).
3. **Honestly graded** — one tag per claim. The grade is the anti-lying mechanism.
   `@designed` `@built` `@build-verified` `@sim-verified` `@runtime-verified`
   `@hw-verified` `@untested` `@hw-untested` `@todo` `@stock`.
   Untested is untested. **Never grade up to look finished.**
4. **Two-way** — the innards carry a greppable back-link to the card, so the wiki is
   bidirectional.

## The triad — three legs, all cross-linked

- **`<name>.feature` (the card)** — the spec: graded verifiable claims, each cited to
  its innards. The *what* + *why-as-grade*.
- **`<name>.session.md`** — the spawning conversation stored beside the card: the
  requests, refinements, corrections, rejected options, the "no I didn't do it"
  admissions. **Faithful, not flattering** — the grade's audit trail. This enables the
  **vibe diff**: across versions you diff the code, the card, AND the dialogue that
  drove each change. A card without its session can spawn the code but not the vibe —
  INCOMPLETE.
  **MANDATORY "How to get back" block** — transcript `file://` path, session ID,
  `Codex --resume <id>`, real date+timestamps pulled from the transcript (never
  fabricated; if unconfirmable, say so). `gen-sessions.py` discovers these repo-wide.
  **MANDATORY bundle, don't just link** — a `file://` link rots the moment the
  `.jsonl` moves. Copy the raw transcript beside the card as
  `<name>.transcript.jsonl` (lossless) plus a readable `<name>.transcript.md`. The
  curated `.session.md` is the audit; the bundled transcript is the source.
- **RESULT block** (card header) — what actually shipped: feature commit(s), the PR if
  any ("direct-push, no PR" when none), card-authoring commit(s), files changed.
  Verify delivery by first-parent ancestry — don't guess; watch duplicate PR numbers
  across forks. The hooks maintain the running RESULT-LOG under it.

Three legs cross-linked ⇒ the wiki is rebuildable straight from git: load one card →
spec + rationale + diff, no re-reading raw source.

## The card is a generative seed (it comes first)

The card opens with a **WHAT THIS CARD SPAWNS** preamble because it spawns three spaces:

- **Codespace** = the file structure — the card's own files plus the innards layout it
  cites. From the card you can scaffold or re-derive the code.
- **Thinkspace** = the reasoning — held in the `.session` (wrong turns included). Also
  what the vibe diff diffs.
- **Areaspace** = the domain boundary — what the unit owns and must NOT touch, so
  re-spawning stays in-bounds. Make it verifiable with a `@stock` "must not break"
  scenario.

`card ⇒ codespace + areaspace`; `session ⇒ thinkspace`.

## Tests → Features → automatic index (never hand-typed)

The whole point is that **code conveys its own verified status** — a behaviour is
written ONCE and every status view derives from it:

1. **Tests ARE the Features.** A verifiable claim lives once as a graded `Scenario`;
   its `@grade` tags **are** its test status.
2. **Features become the index.** The status view is GENERATED from those tags, run
   automatically by the pre-commit hook, committed alongside the card.
3. **So anyone can confirm** with zero manual labour: tested or not, at what level, and
   where it links (card → innards → commits → session).

**Banned anti-pattern:** hand-maintaining a parallel "what's tested" list. If you catch
yourself typing `runtime-verified` into an index, stop — change the card's tag and let
the index regenerate. A derived view cannot disagree with its source; a hand-kept one
drifts and lies. Generated files carry a `DO NOT EDIT — generated` header.

## Relationship to Convey (`~/work/convey`)

**This skill is the DOCTRINE + SKIN SYSTEM + portable tooling. Convey is the larger
ENGINE.** A report card IS a Convey "Underlying Principle" — a `principles/NNNN-slug/`
folder bound to git. The hooks shipped here are Convey's canonical stamp engine, which
is why `install.sh` and `convey hooks install --target .` are interchangeable for the
hook half.

Mapping (full detail in `~/work/convey/docs/DOCTRINE.md`):

- **Emit a card** = `convey new "<title>" --target <folder> --skin <code|circuit|api|media>`.
- **`.feature`** = stage 1 *Describe*; `convey verify` reconciles the declared grade
  with the actual run and **flags optimism** (OPTIMISTIC / UNVERIFIED) — the anti-lying
  mechanism, automated. Where no runner exists it reports UNRUN and keeps the declared
  grade (never fakes a pass).
- **`.session`** = stage 2 *Sessions* + `convey bundle` copies the lossless transcript
  beside the card and fills "How to get back".
- **RESULT** = stage 3 *Done* (git-derived) + stage 5 *Change*.
- **Two-way back-link** = `convey backlink`. **The wiki** = `convey atlas`.

Use Convey where it's installed; use `scripts/install.sh` for any repo (or machine)
where it isn't. The four properties and three legs are identical either way.

## The card is conversable

The `.feature` is compact distilled text with the bundled session as lossless backing,
so you can hand it to a `file-to-text` → LLM reader and *talk to it*:

```bash
card converse <name>           # resolve by name + fm-converse it (Apple on-device LLM)
card converse <name> --full    # converse over the full bundled transcript
card bundle <name>             # copy + render the spawning session beside the card
card list | show | path        # browse cards
```

`card` lives at `~/work/apple/bin/card`. This is *why* the full session must be
bundled, not merely linked — an `fm-converse` session can't follow a dead `file://`
link, but it can read a sibling file.

**The universality corollary.** The card is the *same skeleton for every file format*,
so the underlying principle of ANY file can be read INTO a card: take a `.lua` tool, a
`.mp4`, a `.sch`, a `.pdf`, a `.wav` — distill what it *does* and *why* into graded
Given/When/Then claims cited to its innards, bundle the session that produced it, and
the card becomes the universal, conversable lens on that file.

## Domain skins (same skeleton)

- **Code** — Gherkin `.feature`; scenarios cite `FILE.ext Proc (~line)` + commit; tags
  for status; back-link comment in the source.
- **Electronics / circuits** — one card per block. `Given Vin = 5.0V, When EN goes
  high, Then Vout settles to 3.3V ±2% within 200µs`; cite parts (`U1 AP2112`, divider
  `R3/R4`, `Cout C7`); grade `@sim-verified @hw-untested`. A whole circuit "already
  contains its report card" = each block ships its card; building the circuit is
  composing cards; the top card is the sum of sub-cards; schematic ⇄ card back-link.
  Pairs with `circuitjs1` / `schematic-to-circuitjs`.
- **API / pipeline / signal chain** — claim = request→response / input→artifact /
  source→processed; cite the endpoint/stage/device; grade by where it's verified.

## Backfilling click-back into an existing session file (retrofit)

When a card/session predates the click-back requirement, identify the spawning
transcript by **content, never by guess**:

1. `cd ~/.Codex/projects/<sanitized-cwd>/` (one `.jsonl` per session), or just run
   `gen-sessions.py` which does the discovery repo-wide.
2. Count fixed-string hits per transcript on distinctive strings from the work:
   `for f in *.jsonl; do echo "$(grep -cF -e "PTN0003" -e "Lackluster" "$f")  $f"; done`
   Use `grep -F` / `rg -F` — **never** a regex with `.*` between literals
   (catastrophic-backtracking ban). Confirm with a second distinct probe (65 vs 11 hits
   is decisive; 7 vs 6 is not).
3. Pull the window: first/last `"timestamp"`; convert UTC → local.
4. Add the **How to get back** block, including an "identified by content, not guessed"
   note with the hit count and a "Backfilled: <date>" line.
5. **Honesty:** never fabricate a session ID. If nothing decisively matches, say so.

## The one honest caveat

For domains with no test runner (16-bit TASM assembly, a bench circuit before hardware
exists), the card's claims are *verifiable-in-principle* — a disciplined human/LLM
checklist and session command until automation glue exists. The wiki value (persistent,
compounding, faithful, loadable-as-command, git-rebuildable) holds on day one
regardless of whether the automation is ever written.

---

Global rule: `~/.Codex/AGENTS.md` § "BUILDING ANY UNIT EMITS ITS REPORT CARD".
Reference instance (94 cards, full triads, live hooks): `esaruoho/impulse-tracker`
`features/` — the repo this machinery was isolated from.

When a card/session predates the click-back requirement, identify the spawning
transcript by **content, never by guess**:

1. `cd ~/.Codex/projects/<sanitized-cwd>/` (one `.jsonl` per session), or just run
   `gen-sessions.py` which does the discovery repo-wide.
2. Count fixed-string hits per transcript on distinctive strings from the work:
   `for f in *.jsonl; do echo "$(grep -cF -e "PTN0003" -e "Lackluster" "$f")  $f"; done`
   Use `grep -F` / `rg -F` — **never** a regex with `.*` between literals
   (catastrophic-backtracking ban). Confirm with a second distinct probe (65 vs 11 hits
   is decisive; 7 vs 6 is not).
3. Pull the window: first/last `"timestamp"`; convert UTC → local.
4. Add the **How to get back** block, including an "identified by content, not guessed"
   note with the hit count and a "Backfilled: <date>" line.
5. **Honesty:** never fabricate a session ID. If nothing decisively matches, say so.

## The one honest caveat

For domains with no test runner (16-bit TASM assembly, a bench circuit before hardware
exists), the card's claims are *verifiable-in-principle* — a disciplined human/LLM
checklist and session command until automation glue exists. The wiki value (persistent,
compounding, faithful, loadable-as-command, git-rebuildable) holds on day one
regardless of whether the automation is ever written.

# Report Card

> Building a unit of anything emits its report card. The card is not documentation
> bolted on after — it is the durable artifact the work is born with, the SEED the
> work spawns from, and the honest, graded, two-way-linked account of what the unit
> does and which of its innards do it. A unit shipped without its card is incomplete.

Domain-agnostic. The skin changes (Gherkin for code, circuit-block Given/When/Then
for electronics, request/response for an API); the skeleton never does.

**This skill ships working machinery, not just doctrine.** If a repo has no card
system, install it — don't hand-write prose that evaporates with the conversation.

---

## DO THIS FIRST — is the machinery present?

```bash
ls features/*.feature 2>/dev/null | head -3   # cards exist?
git config core.hooksPath                     # should print .githooks
```

**No cards / no hooks → install, then card.** One command, idempotent, never commits:

```bash
~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/install.sh            # current repo, features/
~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/install.sh --target /path/to/repo \
    --cards-dir features --title "Foo — Feature Reference"
```

It drops into the repo:

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `features/print-card.py` | cards → `README.md` + printable `dist/` |
| `features/gen-status.py` | cards → `STATUS.md` (the derived test matrix) |
| `features/gen-sessions.py` | Codex transcripts → `SESSIONS.generated.md` |
| `features/cards.conf` | per-repo knobs (title, source extensions, exclusions) |
| `features/TEMPLATE.feature.txt` | the house-style skeleton to copy |
| `features/INDEX.md` | the commit ⇄ card map (the one hand-kept file) |
| `.githooks/pre-commit` + `post-merge` + `report-card-stamp.sh` | the stamp engine |
| `.githooks/pre-commit.local` | repo-local jobs — **yours, never clobbered on reinstall** |
| `core.hooksPath = .githooks` | set for this clone (git won't auto-run committed hooks) |

Then, **every commit onward, with zero effort:** a diff touching a card's `# WATCH:`
symbols stamps a dated RESULT-LOG line into that card *in the same commit*, and a
staged card regenerates `STATUS.md` / `README.md` / `SESSIONS.generated.md` and stages
them too. Mapping is **by symbol, not filename** — touching an unrelated part of a
shared file does not tag every card.

Already installed elsewhere and want the engine refreshed? Re-run `install.sh`; it
overwrites the canonical hooks + generators and keeps `pre-commit.local`, `cards.conf`,
`INDEX.md`, and every card. `--force` to overwrite those too.

## Then: write the card (the same motion as the build)

1. `cp features/TEMPLATE.feature.txt features/<name>.feature` and fill it in.
2. Write `features/<name>.session.md` — the spawning conversation, faithful not
   flattering, with the mandatory **How to get back** block.
3. Back-link the innards: `// REPORT-CARD >> features/<name>.feature` (comment syntax
   of that language).
4. Set the card's `# WATCH:` line to the symbols it owns — that's the hook contract.
5. Enrol it in `features/INDEX.md`.
6. `python3 features/print-card.py --readme` (and `--all` for printable `dist/`).
7. Commit. The hooks do the rest.

**House style, grade ladder, banned anti-patterns:** `reference/house-style.md`.
**Why the format is shaped this way:** `reference/wiki-pattern.md`.

## Just report back to me (works WITHOUT git)

```bash
~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/report.sh --target ~/work/foo
```

Regenerates every derived view and prints an honest summary: card count, scenario
count, grades in use, and the three failure modes that otherwise stay silent —
cards with **no `# WATCH:` line** (the hooks can never stamp them), cards whose
grade is written as a **trailing comment** instead of a Gherkin tag (no generator
counts it, so they show as ungraded), and cards with **no `.session.md`** (broken
triad). Finds the card home automatically (`features/`, `cards/`, `docs/cards`).

**Git is optional.** Cards, generators and all derived views work on a plain
folder — `install.sh` detects a non-git target, installs everything except the
hooks, and says so. Only RESULT-LOG *stamping* needs git, because it has to know
which symbols a diff touched. In a non-git folder you run `report.sh` yourself
instead of a commit doing it for you.

## cards.conf keys

| Key | Effect |
|---|---|
| `title` | heading of the generated reference |
| `readme_file` | target for `--readme` (default `README.md`) — **set this if `features/README.md` is hand-written**, or it gets clobbered |
| `source_ext` | extensions recognised as "innards" in a `# cite:` line |
| `meta_prefix` | card-name prefixes grouped as meta/process cards |
| `exclude` | cards kept out of `STATUS.md` (rollups, host-side tooling) |
| `readme_exclude` | cards hidden from the reference entirely (rare) |
| `grade_map` | translate a repo's OWN grade words into canonical tiers, e.g. `@untested-in-renoise:@runtime-untested, @built:@code-verified` — the project keeps its vocabulary AND gets a correct matrix |
| `runtime_label` / `hardware_label` / `status_note` | STATUS.md column labels + note |
| `sessions_file` | session-registry filename (default `SESSIONS.generated.md`) |
| `project_dirs` | extra paths whose Codex transcripts belong to this repo |

## Card dialects — indented banners are legal

Some repos put the banner **inside** the `Feature:` block, indented (Paketti does).
The stamp engine matches `# WATCH:` / `RESULT-LOG >>` at **line start with leading
whitespace allowed**, so both dialects stamp, and the inserted line copies the
marker's own indentation. What is still rejected is a *mid-sentence* mention of the
marker in prose, so a card describing the convention can't opt itself in.

A strict column-0 anchor is what made every Paketti card a silent no-op for months —
hooks installed, running, stamping nothing, no error. If cards aren't being stamped,
run `report.sh` before assuming the hooks are broken.

## Verification commands

```bash
python3 features/print-card.py --readme     # regenerate the feature reference
python3 features/print-card.py --all        # per-card dist/ (pure Gherkin + printable)
python3 features/gen-status.py              # regenerate the test matrix
python3 features/gen-sessions.py            # regenerate the session registry
rtfc features/dist/<name>.card.md           # printable card → RTF clipboard
```

All are dependency-free Apple-native python3, deterministic (no timestamps embedded,
so no commit churn), and resolve the card home from `--cards-dir` → `$REPORT_CARDS_DIR`
→ the script's own directory.

---

## The four properties (every card, every domain)

1. **Verifiable claims** — condition → action → expected result.
   `Given <state>, When <action>, Then <measurable outcome>`.
2. **Linked to the innards** — each claim cites the exact parts that satisfy it
   (proc + line + commit; component refdes + node; file + function).
3. **Honestly graded** — one tag per claim. The grade is the anti-lying mechanism.
   `@designed` `@built` `@build-verified` `@sim-verified` `@runtime-verified`
   `@hw-verified` `@untested` `@hw-untested` `@todo` `@stock`.
   Untested is untested. **Never grade up to look finished.**
4. **Two-way** — the innards carry a greppable back-link to the card, so the wiki is
   bidirectional.

## The triad — three legs, all cross-linked

- **`<name>.feature` (the card)** — the spec: graded verifiable claims, each cited to
  its innards. The *what* + *why-as-grade*.
- **`<name>.session.md`** — the spawning conversation stored beside the card: the
  requests, refinements, corrections, rejected options, the "no I didn't do it"
  admissions. **Faithful, not flattering** — the grade's audit trail. This enables the
  **vibe diff**: across versions you diff the code, the card, AND the dialogue that
  drove each change. A card without its session can spawn the code but not the vibe —
  INCOMPLETE.
  **MANDATORY "How to get back" block** — transcript `file://` path, session ID,
  `Codex --resume <id>`, real date+timestamps pulled from the transcript (never
  fabricated; if unconfirmable, say so). `gen-sessions.py` discovers these repo-wide.
  **MANDATORY bundle, don't just link** — a `file://` link rots the moment the
  `.jsonl` moves. Copy the raw transcript beside the card as
  `<name>.transcript.jsonl` (lossless) plus a readable `<name>.transcript.md`. The
  curated `.session.md` is the audit; the bundled transcript is the source.
- **RESULT block** (card header) — what actually shipped: feature commit(s), the PR if
  any ("direct-push, no PR" when none), card-authoring commit(s), files changed.
  Verify delivery by first-parent ancestry — don't guess; watch duplicate PR numbers
  across forks. The hooks maintain the running RESULT-LOG under it.

Three legs cross-linked ⇒ the wiki is rebuildable straight from git: load one card →
spec + rationale + diff, no re-reading raw source.

## The card is a generative seed (it comes first)

The card opens with a **WHAT THIS CARD SPAWNS** preamble because it spawns three spaces:

- **Codespace** = the file structure — the card's own files plus the innards layout it
  cites. From the card you can scaffold or re-derive the code.
- **Thinkspace** = the reasoning — held in the `.session` (wrong turns included). Also
  what the vibe diff diffs.
- **Areaspace** = the domain boundary — what the unit owns and must NOT touch, so
  re-spawning stays in-bounds. Make it verifiable with a `@stock` "must not break"
  scenario.

`card ⇒ codespace + areaspace`; `session ⇒ thinkspace`.

## Tests → Features → automatic index (never hand-typed)

The whole point is that **code conveys its own verified status** — a behaviour is
written ONCE and every status view derives from it:

1. **Tests ARE the Features.** A verifiable claim lives once as a graded `Scenario`;
   its `@grade` tags **are** its test status.
2. **Features become the index.** The status view is GENERATED from those tags, run
   automatically by the pre-commit hook, committed alongside the card.
3. **So anyone can confirm** with zero manual labour: tested or not, at what level, and
   where it links (card → innards → commits → session).

**Banned anti-pattern:** hand-maintaining a parallel "what's tested" list. If you catch
yourself typing `runtime-verified` into an index, stop — change the card's tag and let
the index regenerate. A derived view cannot disagree with its source; a hand-kept one
drifts and lies. Generated files carry a `DO NOT EDIT — generated` header.

## Relationship to Convey (`~/work/convey`)

**This skill is the DOCTRINE + SKIN SYSTEM + portable tooling. Convey is the larger
ENGINE.** A report card IS a Convey "Underlying Principle" — a `principles/NNNN-slug/`
folder bound to git. The hooks shipped here are Convey's canonical stamp engine, which
is why `install.sh` and `convey hooks install --target .` are interchangeable for the
hook half.

Mapping (full detail in `~/work/convey/docs/DOCTRINE.md`):

- **Emit a card** = `convey new "<title>" --target <folder> --skin <code|circuit|api|media>`.
- **`.feature`** = stage 1 *Describe*; `convey verify` reconciles the declared grade
  with the actual run and **flags optimism** (OPTIMISTIC / UNVERIFIED) — the anti-lying
  mechanism, automated. Where no runner exists it reports UNRUN and keeps the declared
  grade (never fakes a pass).
- **`.session`** = stage 2 *Sessions* + `convey bundle` copies the lossless transcript
  beside the card and fills "How to get back".
- **RESULT** = stage 3 *Done* (git-derived) + stage 5 *Change*.
- **Two-way back-link** = `convey backlink`. **The wiki** = `convey atlas`.

Use Convey where it's installed; use `scripts/install.sh` for any repo (or machine)
where it isn't. The four properties and three legs are identical either way.

## The card is conversable

The `.feature` is compact distilled text with the bundled session as lossless backing,
so you can hand it to a `file-to-text` → LLM reader and *talk to it*:

```bash
card converse <name>           # resolve by name + fm-converse it (Apple on-device LLM)
card converse <name> --full    # converse over the full bundled transcript
card bundle <name>             # copy + render the spawning session beside the card
card list | show | path        # browse cards
```

`card` lives at `~/work/apple/bin/card`. This is *why* the full session must be
bundled, not merely linked — an `fm-converse` session can't follow a dead `file://`
link, but it can read a sibling file.

**The universality corollary.** The card is the *same skeleton for every file format*,
so the underlying principle of ANY file can be read INTO a card: take a `.lua` tool, a
`.mp4`, a `.sch`, a `.pdf`, a `.wav` — distill what it *does* and *why* into graded
Given/When/Then claims cited to its innards, bundle the session that produced it, and
the card becomes the universal, conversable lens on that file.

## Domain skins (same skeleton)

- **Code** — Gherkin `.feature`; scenarios cite `FILE.ext Proc (~line)` + commit; tags
  for status; back-link comment in the source.
- **Electronics / circuits** — one card per block. `Given Vin = 5.0V, When EN goes
  high, Then Vout settles to 3.3V ±2% within 200µs`; cite parts (`U1 AP2112`, divider
  `R3/R4`, `Cout C7`); grade `@sim-verified @hw-untested`. A whole circuit "already
  contains its report card" = each block ships its card; building the circuit is
  composing cards; the top card is the sum of sub-cards; schematic ⇄ card back-link.
  Pairs with `circuitjs1` / `schematic-to-circuitjs`.
- **API / pipeline / signal chain** — claim = request→response / input→artifact /
  source→processed; cite the endpoint/stage/device; grade by where it's verified.

## Backfilling click-back into an existing session file (retrofit)

When a card/session predates the click-back requirement, identify the spawning
transcript by **content, never by guess**:

1. `cd ~/.Codex/projects/<sanitized-cwd>/` (one `.jsonl` per session), or just run
   `gen-sessions.py` which does the discovery repo-wide.
2. Count fixed-string hits per transcript on distinctive strings from the work:
   `for f in *.jsonl; do echo "$(grep -cF -e "PTN0003" -e "Lackluster" "$f")  $f"; done`
   Use `grep -F` / `rg -F` — **never** a regex with `.*` between literals
   (catastrophic-backtracking ban). Confirm with a second distinct probe (65 vs 11 hits
   is decisive; 7 vs 6 is not).
3. Pull the window: first/last `"timestamp"`; convert UTC → local.
4. Add the **How to get back** block, including an "identified by content, not guessed"
   note with the hit count and a "Backfilled: <date>" line.
5. **Honesty:** never fabricate a session ID. If nothing decisively matches, say so.

## The one honest caveat

For domains with no test runner (16-bit TASM assembly, a bench circuit before hardware
exists), the card's claims are *verifiable-in-principle* — a disciplined human/LLM
checklist and session command until automation glue exists. The wiki value (persistent,
compounding, faithful, loadable-as-command, git-rebuildable) holds on day one
regardless of whether the automation is ever written.

---

Global rule: `~/.Codex/AGENTS.md` § "BUILDING ANY UNIT EMITS ITS REPORT CARD".
Reference instance (94 cards, full triads, live hooks): `esaruoho/impulse-tracker`
`features/` — the repo this machinery was isolated from.
"}

                pakettiShowLargestSamplesDialogDialog()

              end
              
              PakettiRestoreNewSampleMonitoring(AutoSamplifyMonitoringState)
            end
            
            slicer = ProcessSlicer(process_func)
            progress_dialog, progress_vb = slicer:create_dialog("Trimming Sample by Half")
            slicer:start()
          end
        },
        
        vb:button{
          width=50,
          text="Delete",

-- Core function to duplicate track and instrument with configurable options
-- Parameters:
--   copy_dsp: boolean - whether to copy DSP devices
--   copy_automation: boolean - whether to copy automation
--   jump_to_editor: boolean - whether to jump to Sample Editor and/or open External Editor
function duplicateTrackAndInstrumentCore(copy_dsp, copy_automation, jump_to_editor)
  local song = renoise.song()
  local track_index = song.selected_track_index
  local selected_track = song:track(track_index)
  
  -- Protection: Check if current track is a send track (or master/group track)
  if selected_track.type ~= renoise.Track.TRACK_TYPE_SEQUENCER then
    local track_type_name = ""
    if selected_track.type == renoise.Track.TRACK_TYPE_SEND then
      track_type_name = "send"
    elseif selected_track.type == renoise.Track.TRACK_TYPE_MASTER then
      track_type_name = "master"
    elseif selected_track.type == renoise.Track.TRACK_TYPE_GROUP then
      track_type_name = "group"
    else
      track_type_name = "non-sequencer"
    end
    renoise.app():show_status("Cannot duplicate " .. track_type_name .. " tracks. Please select a sequencer track.")
    return
  end
  
  -- First, duplicate the instrument
  local instrument_index = song.selected_instrument_index
  local original_instrument = song.instruments[instrument_index]
  
  -- Store external editor state and close it temporarily if needed
  local external_editor_open = false
  if original_instrument.plugin_properties and original_instrument.plugin_properties.plugin_device then
    external_editor_open = original_instrument.plugin_properties.plugin_device.external_editor_visible
    if external_editor_open then
      original_instrument.plugin_properties.plugin_device.external_editor_visible = false
    end
  end

  -- Insert and copy the instrument
  if not safeInsertInstrumentAt(song, instrument_index + 1) then return end
  local new_instrument = song.instruments[instrument_index + 1]
  new_instrument:copy_from(original_instrument)

  -- Copy phrases if they exist
  if #original_instrument.phrases > 0 then
    local existing_phrases = #new_instrument.phrases
    local phrases_to_copy = #original_instrument.phrases
    if existing_phrases + phrases_to_copy > 126 then
      error("Cannot copy phrases: Would exceed maximum of 126 phrases per instrument (currently has " .. existing_phrases .. ", trying to add " .. phrases_to_copy .. ")")
    end
    for phrase_index = 1, #original_instrument.phrases do
      new_instrument:insert_phrase_at(phrase_index)
      new_instrument.phrases[phrase_index]:copy_from(original_instrument.phrases[phrase_index])
    end
  end
  
  -- Create new track
  song:insert_track_at(track_index + 1)
  local new_track = song:track(track_index + 1)
  
  -- Copy track settings
  new_track.visible_note_columns = selected_track.visible_note_columns
  new_track.visible_effect_columns = selected_track.visible_effect_columns
  new_track.volume_column_visible = selected_track.volume_column_visible
  new_track.panning_column_visible = selected_track.panning_column_visible
  new_track.delay_column_visible = selected_track.delay_column_visible
  new_track.sample_effects_column_visible = selected_track.sample_effects_column_visible
  new_track.collapsed = selected_track.collapsed
  
  -- Copy mixer volume settings
  new_track.prefx_volume.value = selected_track.prefx_volume.value
  new_track.postfx_volume.value = selected_track.postfx_volume.value
  
  -- Copy DSP devices and their settings (if enabled)
  if copy_dsp then
    for device_index = 2, #selected_track.devices do  -- Start from 2 to skip Track Volume device
      local old_device = selected_track.devices[device_index]
      local new_device = new_track:insert_device_at(old_device.device_path, device_index)
      -- Copy device parameters and mixer settings
      for param_index = 1, #old_device.parameters do
        new_device.parameters[param_index].value = old_device.parameters[param_index].value
        new_device.parameters[param_index].show_in_mixer = old_device.parameters[param_index].show_in_mixer
      end
      -- Copy device display settings
      new_device.is_maximized = old_device.is_maximized
      -- Handle Instrument Automation device specially
      if old_device.device_path:find("Instr. Automation") then
        local old_xml = old_device.active_preset_data
        local new_xml = old_xml:gsub("<instrument>(%d+)</instrument>", 
          function(instr_index)
            return string.format("<instrument>%d</instrument>", instrument_index)
          end)
        new_device.active_preset_data = new_xml
      end
    end
  end
  
  -- Copy pattern data and update instrument references
  for pattern_index = 1, #song.patterns do
    local pattern = song:pattern(pattern_index)
    local source_track = pattern:track(track_index)
    local dest_track = pattern:track(track_index + 1)
    
    -- Copy all lines
    for line_index = 1, pattern.number_of_lines do
      dest_track:line(line_index):copy_from(source_track:line(line_index))
      -- Update instrument references in note columns
      for _, note_column in ipairs(dest_track:line(line_index).note_columns) do
        if note_column.instrument_value ~= 255 then  -- Skip empty instrument values
          note_column.instrument_value = instrument_index
        end
      end
    end
    
    -- Copy automation data (if enabled)
    if copy_automation then
      for _, automation in ipairs(source_track.automation) do
        local new_automation = dest_track:create_automation(automation.dest_parameter)
        new_automation:copy_from(automation)
      end
    end
  end
  
  -- Select the new track and instrument
  song.selected_track_index = track_index + 1
  song.selected_instrument_index = instrument_index + 1
  
  -- Check if instrument has samples and plugin (for jump and status)
  local has_samples = #new_instrument.samples > 0 and new_instrument.samples[1].sample_buffer.has_sample_data
  local has_plugin = new_instrument.plugin_properties and new_instrument.plugin_properties.plugin_device
  
  -- Handle editor visibility based on jump_to_editor parameter
  if jump_to_editor then
    -- Jump to Sample Editor if there are samples
    if has_samples then
      renoise.app().window.active_middle_frame = renoise.ApplicationWindow.MIDDLE_FRAME_INSTRUMENT_SAMPLE_EDITOR
    end
    -- Open External Editor if there's a plugin
    if has_plugin then
      new_instrument.plugin_properties.plugin_device.external_editor_visible = true
    end
  else
    -- Restore external editor state if needed (original behavior)
    if external_editor_open and has_plugin then
      new_instrument.plugin_properties.plugin_device.external_editor_visible = true
    end
  end
  
  -- Build status message
  local status_parts = {"Track and instrument duplicated"}
  if not copy_dsp and not copy_automation then
    status_parts[1] = "Track and instrument duplicated (clean)"
  end
  if jump_to_editor then
    if has_samples then
      table.insert(status_parts, "Sample Editor opened")
    end
    if has_plugin then
      table.insert(status_parts, "External Editor opened")
    end
  end
  renoise.app():show_status(table.concat(status_parts, ", "))
end
